Pumpkin Maple Caramel Crunch Cake (Scoop Cake)

By Lisa Kitahara

on Oct 09, 2026

PinShareJump to Recipe

This Pumpkin Caramel Crunch Scoop Cake layers tender pumpkin bread with brown butter maple diplomat cream, kabocha caramel, and a smooth sour cream ganache. Finished with crisp maple cornflake crunch, it’s an easy make-ahead pumpkin dessert that’s perfect for fall gatherings, holidays, or simply enjoying straight from the fridge.

Pumpkin Scoop Cake with Leftovers

Why You’ll Love This Recipe

  • Uses leftover pumpkin bread: If you have a few slices of pumpkin bread sitting around, this is one of my favourite ways to turn them into an entirely new dessert. The pumpkin bread becomes soft and cake-like as it chills with all the creamy layers.
  • Great for making ahead: Every component can be prepared ahead of time, and can even be frozen. The assembled scoop cake is actually best made a day in advance so the layers have time to chill and the pumpkin bread can absorb some of the caramel and cream.
  • No cake decorating but still impressive: There is no stacking, frosting, piping, or trying to get perfectly even cake layers. Everything gets layered into one dish, making this a much easier alternative to a decorated cake.
  • It is incredibly delicious: The combination of pumpkin bread, salted caramel, brown butter maple cream, tangy sour cream ganache, and crunchy maple cornflakes is seriously hard to resist. You get something creamy, soft, chewy, crunchy, salty, and sweet in every scoop.

Ingredients and Substitutions

Here are the ingredients you’ll need to make this pumpkin scoop cake. Each component brings a different texture and flavour, so I recommend making the recipe as written the first time.

  • Pumpkin bread: Homemade or store-bought pumpkin bread works. I love using my Salted Maple Pumpkin Bread because the maple and salted flavours pair especially well with the caramel and cream.
  • Maple syrup: Adds sweetness and a warm maple flavour to the diplomat cream and crunch.
  • Whole milk: The base of the pastry cream. Whole milk gives the cream a richer, smoother texture.
  • Egg yolks: Help thicken and enrich the diplomat cream.
  • Cornstarch: Thickens the pastry cream and gives it enough structure to hold between the layers.
  • Butter: Used for the brown butter diplomat cream and maple cornflake crunch. Browning it adds a deeper, nutty flavour that really brings this scoop cake together.
  • Milk powder: Adds extra nuttiness to the pastry cream.
  • Heavy cream: Used to lighten the pastry cream into a soft, creamy diplomat cream.
  • White chocolate: Used for the sour cream ganache, adding sweetness and structure.
  • Sour cream: Balances the sweetness of the white chocolate with a little tang.
  • Cornflakes: The base of the maple crunch. They add the crispy texture that makes this scoop cake so good.
  • Brown sugar: Adds caramel-like sweetness to the crunch.

How to Make Pumpkin Caramel Crunch Scoop Cake

This dessert is made by preparing each component separately, then layering everything into a small baking dish before chilling until set.

  1. Make the brown butter maple custard cream: Brown the butter and set aside. Caramelize the maple syrup, then heat the milk. Whisk together the egg yolks, cornstarch, and salt, then gradually whisk in the hot milk. Cook until the custard thickens, then whisk in the brown butter and vanilla. Cover and cool completely.
  2. Make the kabocha caramel: Grind the nuts, then blend them with the caramel and kabocha until smooth and creamy.
  3. Make the brown butter maple diplomat cream: Whisk or use an immersion blender to smooth out the chilled custard cream. Whip the heavy cream to medium-stiff peaks, then gently fold it into the custard cream until smooth.
  4. Layer the scoop cake: Add pieces of pumpkin bread to your dish, followed by the diplomat cream and kabocha caramel. Repeat the layers, then cover and refrigerate.
  5. Make the maple cornflake crunch: Toss the cornflakes with the heated butter, maple syrup, brown sugar, milk powder, salt, and vanilla. Bake until crisp and caramelized, then cool completely.
  6. Make the sour cream ganache: Melt the white chocolate and mix with the sour cream until smooth and creamy. Pour over the chilled scoop cake and gently tilt the dish so it spreads into an even layer.
  7. Chill: Cover and refrigerate overnight. This gives the pumpkin bread time to soften and absorb the flavours from the surrounding layers while the creams set.
  8. Finish and serve: Add the maple cornflake crunch just before serving for the best contrast between the soft, creamy cake and crisp topping.

Lisa’s Recipe Tips

  1. Make it the day before: This is one of those desserts that gets better after sitting overnight. The pumpkin bread softens slightly and becomes almost cake-pudding-like while still holding enough structure to scoop.
  2. Let the components cool before assembling. The caramel, diplomat cream, and ganache should be cooled before layering so they don’t melt or loosen the other components.
  3. Keep the crunch separate if making it ahead: For the best texture, store some of the maple cornflake crunch separately and add it right before serving. This keeps it crisp instead of letting it soften in the cream.
  4. Don’t worry about perfect layers: This is a scoop cake, so everything is meant to be rustic. Cut the pumpkin bread into pieces that fit your dish and layer everything wherever it fits.

Variations

You can easily make this into individual desserts by layering everything into small cups or jars for single servings. I love doing this for home cafes, parties and potlucks.

And honestly, as long as you have pumpkin bread, some kind of custard or cream (even whipped cream!), and caramel sauce, you can really make your own version. I’ve made this with hojicha diplomat cream and blonde chocolate ganache before, and it was incredible. Go wild with the flavours! I do recommend making the crunch, though, because that crispy layer really adds so much to the cake.

Have banana bread instead? Try my Banana Bread Crunch Scoop Cake. Or if you’re craving chocolate, try my Chocolate Crunch Tiramisu.

Serving Suggestions

I like serving this scoop cake chilled, straight from the refrigerator. Scoop it into small bowls or dessert glasses, making sure to get a little bit of everything in each serving.

For the best texture, add a generous handful of the maple cornflake crunch right before serving. The contrast between the cold, creamy layers and the crisp caramelized cornflakes is one of my favourite parts!

How to Store Pumpkin Crunch Cake

Store the assembled scoop cake covered in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For the best texture, keep any extra maple cornflake crunch in an airtight container at room temperature and add it just before serving.

You can also freeze leftovers. Wrap the scoop cake tightly in cling wrap, or portion it into individual servings and wrap each one separately. When ready to eat, thaw in the refrigerator and enjoy chilled.

Recipe FAQ

Can I make scoop cake ahead of time?

Yes, and I actually recommend it. Assemble the cake the day before serving and refrigerate overnight. This gives the pumpkin bread time to absorb some of the caramel and cream and allows all the flavours to come together.

Can I use store bought pumpkin bread?

Sure! Homemade pumpkin bread is my preference, but store-bought pumpkin bread works well too. If possible, choose a loaf that is soft and moist but still sturdy enough to cut into pieces.

Can I use store bought caramel sauce?

Absolutely! You can skip making the kabocha caramel and use your favourite store-bought caramel sauce instead. You’ll miss some of the nuttiness from the sesame and almonds, though, so you can stir a few tablespoons of almond butter or tahini into the caramel sauce to bring some of that flavour back. Alternatively, add some chopped nuts to the maple cornflake crunch.

Can I freeze the components?

Yes. The custard cream, kabocha caramel, pumpkin bread and cornflake crunch can all be made ahead of time and frozen. After assembling the cake, you can freeze it too.

Pumpkin Caramel Crunch Cake

5 Stars 4 Stars 3 Stars 2 Stars 1 Star

No reviews

  • Author: Lisa Kitahara
  • Total Time: 55 minutes
  • Yield: 1200 ml container
  • Diet: Vegetarian
Print Recipe
Pin Recipe

Description

This Pumpkin Caramel Crunch Scoop Cake layers tender pumpkin bread with brown butter maple diplomat cream, kabocha caramel, and a smooth sour cream ganache. Finished with crisp maple cornflake crunch, it’s an easy make-ahead pumpkin dessert that’s perfect for fall gatherings, holidays, or simply enjoying straight from the fridge.

Ingredients

Units

Brown Butter Pastry Cream

  • 37 g salted butter
  • 6 g milk powder
  • 200 ml whole milk
  • 50 g pure maple syrup
  • 35 g egg yolks (about 2 yolks)
  • 16 g cornstarch
  • 1/8 tsp kosher salt
  • 1/2 vanilla bean pod or 1 tsp vanilla paste

Brown Butter Diplomat Cream

  • 120 g heavy cream

Kabocha Caramel

  • 50 g white sesame seeds
  • 50 g almonds/cashews
  • 80 g miso caramel sauce
  • 40 g cooked kabocha

Maple Cornflake Crunch

  • 70 g cornflakes
  • 35 g salted butter
  • 45 g pure maple syrup
  • 20 g light brown sugar
  • 10 g milk powder
  • 1/8 tsp kosher salt (use 1/4 tsp if using unsalted butter)
  • 1/2 tsp vanilla extract

Sour Cream Ganache

  • 90 g white chocolate
  • 60 g sour cream

Assembly

  • 265–300 g pumpkin bread, about 4-6 slices 1-1.5 cm thick
  • strong brewed coffee, optional

Instructions

Preliminary Notes

  • I used a 7 x 3H inch round dish that holds 1200 ml.
  • You can use any pumpkin bread but I used my salted maple pumpkin bread that is very moist. If using older or dry pumpkin bread (ie. the end bits) I recommend brushing some coffee or simple syrup to add a bit more moisture back.
  • For more in depth tutorial on making brown butter please read my How to Brown butter Post.
  • For more details on how to make custard cream and diplomat cream, please read my custard cream recipe and diplomat cream recipe.

Brown Butter Maple Pastry Cream

  1. Melt the butter and milk powder in a saucepan over medium heat. Continue cooking, stirring frequently, until the butter turns deeply golden brown and smells nutty. Immediately pour into a separate bowl to stop the cooking. Set aside to cool slightly.
  2. Add the maple syrup to a small saucepan over medium heat. Let it simmer, swirling occasionally, until noticeably darker and caramelized, about 2–3 minutes. Do not cook it until very thick or burnt.
  3. Slowly whisk the warm milk into the maple syrup. It will bubble aggressively and the maple may briefly seize. Keep whisking until the mixture comes back together and is smooth.
  4. In a bowl, whisk the egg yolks, cornstarch, and salt until smooth. Slowly whisk the hot maple-milk mixture into the yolk mixture. Pour everything back into the saucepan.
  5. Cook over medium-low heat, whisking constantly, until thickened and large bubbles begin breaking through the surface. The pastry cream should be thick and glossy.
  6. Remove from the heat and whisk in the browned butter until completely smooth and emulsified. Transfer to a bowl, cover the surface directly with plastic wrap, and place an ice pack on top to speed up cooling. Once no longer hot, refrigerate until completely chilled and ready to use.

Make the Kabocha Caramel

  1. In a high speed blender add the sesame and cashews and blend until ground. Add the caramel and kabocha and blend until smooth, scraping down the sides as needed. Transfer 1/4 cup (60 g) to a piping bag and add remaining to a air tight container. Keep refrigerated.

Brown Butter Diplomat Cream

  1. Whisk the chilled pastry cream until smooth. If its lumpy use a immersion blender to blend until smooth. In a separate bowl, whip the heavy cream to medium-stiff peaks. Gently fold the whipped cream into the pastry cream in 2-3 additions until smooth and light.

Assembly

  1. Arrange the pumpkin bread slices in the bottom of your dish, slicing them as needed to create an even layer. Spread with half of the brown butter diplomat cream, then drizzle half of the kabocha caramel on top.
  2. Repeat with another layer of pumpkin bread, the remaining diplomat cream, and the remaining kabocha caramel.
  3. Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour to allow the cake to set.

Maple Cornflake Crunch

  1. Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Melt the butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Add the maple syrup, brown sugar, milk powder, salt, and vanilla. Stir until smooth and combined.
  2. Place the cornflakes in a bowl and pour the butter mixture over them. Gently toss until evenly coated, taking care not to crush the cornflakes too much.
  3. Spread the coated cornflakes onto a parchment-lined baking sheet. Bake for 10-15 minutes, stirring once halfway through, until golden and crisp. Let cool completely. The crunch will become crispier as it cools.

Sour Cream Ganache

  1. Melt the white chocolate gently in the microwave in short intervals, stirring between each, or over a double boiler. Once smooth, add the sour cream and stir until completely combined and glossy.

Finishing

  1. Pour the sour cream ganache over the chilled cake. Gently tilt the dish to spread the ganache into an even layer.
  2. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or until the ganache is set.
  3. Just before serving, top with the maple cornflake crunch. I recommend adding only as much crunch as you plan to serve, since it will soften as it sits in the refrigerator.

  • Cook Time: 20 minutes
